roles.name: connectivity
roles.persona: the desk's connection to a broker or venue
roles.summary: Connects the firm to a broker or venue, sending placements in the venue's own form and reporting what the venue says.

duties.duty: Sends placements in the venue's own form, converting at the edge.
Reports what the venue says, as it says it -- acknowledgements, rejections, changes, fills, busts, charges and a restatement's reason.
Where it provides market access, declares and runs the firm's pre-trade risk checks, and sends nothing that fails them.
Keeps the venue's raw messages and session state in its own storage, to reconnect and resend.
Is linked to one ems and sends only its placements, with what that ems set in the venue's account field, linking no accounts of its own (contract v22).

leaves_to.what: what to trade and how much
choosing venues and splitting, and the venue's account field
the order's state, which the book decides

roles.name: compliance
roles.summary: Checks acts against the firm's rules before and after the trade, each verdict naming what it checked, and posts standing approved limits execution may act within.

duties.duty: Records a verdict on each act it checks, naming the version of the order or placement it checked.
Sets the limits of a mandate and the firm-wide credit limits a market-access connectivity plugin enforces.
In the fast and high-frequency tiers, posts standing approved limits execution may act within, in place of a verdict on each order.
Raises post-trade alerts, which are the kernel's records, not its own storage.

leaves_to.what: stopping trading other than as the gate, by its verdicts

roles.name: custody
roles.persona: the operations staff who rely on what a custodian, prime broker or broker says
roles.summary: Brings a custodian's, prime broker's or broker's statements, positions and cash into the street store, and keeps its own connection complete.

duties.duty: Reports the external accounts a connection reaches and its sync state.
Opens a statement per account, records each holding as the custodian reports it, and closes the statement.
Resolves the identifiers it reads, and reports an instrument it could not resolve; it never mints reference data.
Links the external accounts it reaches to the deployment's accounts, on its admin page.
Keeps its own connection complete, every account reached and every statement taken, and keeps the custodian's raw records in its own storage.

Converts the custodian's codes into the contract's values at the edge: each account's kind, each holding's asset class and type. A code it cannot convert it sends as not known, with the custodian's code beside it as reported, and never as the nearest value.

Counts each asset once: the cash of a currency net of any holding the custodian also counts as cash, netted by its own named rule; and withholds, saying why on its page, a statement it cannot serve clean.

States every holding's settled quantity and its pending quantities by value date, and names the custodian of every statement; what the custodian does not send it closes itself, by better input, a second source of its own, its page or a named rule, each value with its provenance and never presented as the custodian's.
References, on every row it sends, the raw record the row was converted from; the reference is followed only through its own page.
Passes the custody suite in full: a plugin that falls short of the role is not verified, and declares nothing about what it supports.

leaves_to.what: reconciling the book with the street

roles.name: data
roles.summary: Puts market, reference and alternative data into the lake, its vendor's codes converted into the platform's attributes.

duties.duty: Puts market, reference and alternative data into the lake, converting its vendor's codes at the edge.

Resolves the subjects and venues its source names, reads an instrument's record to name to its vendor one another source resolved, and reports what it could not resolve; it never mints reference data.
Keeps its vendor's raw files and cursors in its own storage.

leaves_to.what: identity, which the platform master mints at the instrument store's request (decisions/037, from contract v24)

roles.name: ems
roles.summary: Works orders across venues, creating placements and coordinating requests for quote.

duties.duty: Works orders across venues and creates placements.
Coordinates a request for quote across dealers.
Works a dealer-side quote once portfolio has decided to quote.
Proposes child orders under a released order in its account for its in-house strategies, each split from its parent (contract v22).
Places through the connectivity plugins linked to it, usually as a desk, setting what each placement sends in the venue's account field from its map of accounts to venue account codes (contract v22).

leaves_to.what: what to trade and how much
changing an ordered quantity, which it never does

roles.name: confirmation
roles.summary: Confirms and affirms trades with external matching services.

duties.duty: Confirms and affirms trades with external matching services, in a later slice.
Keeps the matching service's raw messages in its own storage.

roles.name: oms
roles.persona: the trader or desk managing orders
roles.summary: Works committed orders -- merging and splitting, coordinating compliance checks, setting execution instructions -- and books and hands them off.

duties.duty: Works committed orders, merging and splitting them.
Coordinates compliance checks and releases orders.
Sets execution instructions, and selects tax lots.
Books executions and hands bookings off to operations.

roles.name: operations
roles.summary: Keeps the book right after the trade -- opening balances, adjustments, reconciliation with the street, allocations after the hand-off and transfers.

duties.duty: Records an account's opening balance and the book's adjustments, each with its reason.
Reconciles the book with the street daily, each difference a break.
Owns allocations after the hand-off, and corrects bookings after it.
Proposes and releases transfers.

roles.name: portfolio
roles.persona: the portfolio manager; on the sell side, the salesperson as the client's manager's proxy; a market-making strategy
roles.summary: Makes the investment decision -- what and how much -- specifying portfolio parameters, risk analytics and proposed trades' overlap with the common optimiser and analytics components, and proposes orders and allocation instructions.

duties.duty: Decides what to trade and how much, and proposes orders.
Sets and amends the allocation instruction.
Decides to quote, pass or reject on the dealer side.
As an intake receiving clients' orders, or an outsourced trading desk, keeps its raw messages in its own storage (contract v22).

leaves_to.what: its own mandate's limits, so it cannot grant itself its envelope

roles.name: reporting
roles.persona: whoever reads results: managers, clients, risk, regulators
roles.archetype: Reporting, analytics and valuation, and an outbound edge
roles.summary: Specifies and shows reports and analyses, the common analytics component computing them; sends reports and regulatory submissions out, keeping them as sent.

duties.duty: Values and reports what the firm holds and did.
Sends reports and regulatory submissions to the outside, keeping them as sent in its own storage.

roles.name: servicing
roles.summary: Handles corporate actions, lifecycle events and coupons.

duties.duty: Announces corporate actions, lifecycle events and coupons, in a later slice.
Keeps its sources' raw notices in its own storage.

leaves_to.what: booking and positions, which operations records in the book

roles.name: settlement
roles.summary: Transmits a transfer it is named on over an external settlement rail and reports the outcome.

duties.duty: Transmits a transfer it is named on and reports its outcome.
Keeps the rail's raw messages in its own storage.

roles.name: signal
roles.persona: research, a quant, an enterprise data manager -- a person's or an agent's
roles.summary: Generates signals, masters data in the lake from several sources and creates scenario definitions.

duties.duty: Generates signals.
Masters data in the lake from several sources.
Creates scenario definitions.

roles.name: reference
roles.persona: a firm's reference-data team, or an enterprise data management vendor's agent
roles.summary: Gathers a security's terms from sources, reconciles them and fills its template, offering each value to the instrument store with its provenance.

duties.duty: Gathers a security's terms from sources -- vendor fields arriving through data plugins, custodians' reports -- and reconciles them.
Fills a security's template, offering each value with its provenance, itself the source (W3.23).
Reads the template catalogue and the records it fills, resolves a security read-only, and hears the replacements, following each record it holds to the one it became (W3.1, W3.6, W3.22, W3.24).

leaves_to.what: deciding a value: a person accepts an offer
matching or minting an ID: core decides when a record has something to ask by, and the conductor sends it; the platform mints from its own source's values
defining a template, which the platform authors

an aggregator of brokerage accounts that also trades

people.says: People are not roles. Who may use a plugin is a person's level on a role of it, granted by a deployment admin in access groups: write on a plugin's operations and read on its custody, say. A plugin never grants it, and an agent never reaches for a role to give a person access.

levels.says: sees what the plugin shows for that role
also acts through the plugin in that role
administers that role's side of the plugin: its settings and admin pages

philosophy.principle: The roles are fixed and their grants generated; nobody changes them for one plugin.
philosophy.says: A request that needs a grant no role has is reshaped, or becomes a request to revise the contract for every plugin of that role.

philosophy.principle: A grant is the minimum a job function needs, and several roles may hold one row.
philosophy.says: A role is chosen for its duty, not for a grant it happens to hold.

philosophy.principle: A plugin talks only to its sidecar.
philosophy.says: Never to the bus, to another plugin, or to another plugin's storage.

philosophy.principle: Vendor knowledge stops at the plugin.
philosophy.says: Convert at the edge, declare coverage, keep a vendor's mechanics to yourself; what the contract lacks grows the contract, in terms that name no vendor.

philosophy.principle: Core records; it does not police.
philosophy.says: Core is general and plugins are specific. A plugin may narrow what core allows, never widen what it forbids.
The street is what custodians say. The book is verified against it daily, and never overwritten by it.

philosophy.principle: Ownership passes at two hand-offs, and the owner closes a gap.
philosophy.says: Ordered equals allocated from portfolio to oms; executed equals allocated from oms to operations. A gap is answered by the role that owns it, under separation of duties.

philosophy.principle: An optimiser proposes; it never orders.
philosophy.says: A what-if trade reaches the book only by being proposed.

philosophy.principle: Stateless compute; storage only at the edge.
philosophy.says: A plugin holds nothing it cannot lose. An edge role may own storage for its raw external records, and that storage is never a channel to another plugin.

philosophy.principle: People's access is the deployment's to grant.
philosophy.says: read, write or admin, per role of a plugin, by a deployment admin. No plugin administers the deployment.

philosophy.principle: Identity is the deployment's own, and deployment data never reaches the central plane.
philosophy.says: A plugin resolves identifiers and reports what it could not resolve; it never mints an instrument's or an entity's identity. The deployment's instrument store mints its own IDs and matches what plugins report to them, a person at the dashboard completes and merges them, and a global ID the platform holds joins a record as an identifier, never as its key (decisions/030, accepted 2026-10-02).

philosophy.principle: Every action is a typed operation a person could take; automation is a plugin's, chosen by the user.
philosophy.says: Core offers only typed operations, each one something a person could do by hand. Automating them (closing a cleared break, assigning, resolving by policy) is a plugin's behaviour, built from those same operations, off until the user turns it on for their workflow, and run as a service account a plugin admin set up, so the journal says who acted.

philosophy.principle: A plugin sees only the accounts and the users granted access to it.
philosophy.says: No plugin reads the firm's whole account list or user list; each sees the accounts in its own scope, and the people granted access to it on them.

philosophy.principle: The common data model sets the standard; a plugin conforms to it.
philosophy.says: Specific, accurate and interpretable: a plugin sends what its source states, in the model's fields, and leaves a field empty rather than guess; the model does not loosen to fit a vendor.

method.step: Restate the request as acts and data.
method.says: What the plugin must cause, what it must read or hear, what it shows and to whom, what it keeps.
An act that breaks a principle is reshaped before any role is chosen: name the principle and the shape that fits.

method.step: Give each act to the role whose duty owns it.
method.says: From the roles' duties and what each leaves to another, not to a role whose scope merely includes it.

method.step: Give each datum to the least role among those that act.
method.says: Or, where no chosen role reads it, to the role whose duty needs it.

method.step: Take the union, and drop a role another chosen role already covers.
method.says: Keep two duties in two plugins where separation of duties needs it (principle 7), and say which other plugins the deployment must already run.
For each row needed, does the contract version the SDK pins grant it? If not, say what brings it, or that the contract lacks it and a revision would have to add it, in terms that name no vendor.
Who uses the plugin, and at which level.

examples.why: Valuation is reporting's duty: it reads the book's positions and the lake's prices. Not portfolio, since no decision is made; not operations, which writes the book, and whose street is the custodian's view rather than the firm's.

needs.pending: the market data revision, after the book's

examples.available: The book's positions from v8, each lot with its cost and acquisition date from v9; prices with the market data revision. Until then a value cannot be shown from the platform's own prices, and an agent says so.

examples.request: Rebalance my accounts to a model
examples.why: Comparing targets with positions and proposing orders is the investment decision. One vendor's plugin may hold portfolio, oms and ems for unattended trading, and the duties stay separate in the records; the mandate's limits stay compliance's.
examples.deployment_needs: an oms plugin to work the orders and a connectivity plugin for the broker
examples.available: Positions at v8; orders from v22, the order path's first revision. Until a common model language exists, the model is the plugin's own data and does not move with the firm.

examples.request: Trade bonds by request for quote
examples.why: ems, or connectivity, or both. Coordinating a request for quote across dealers is ems's; speaking to the venue that carries it is connectivity's. A trader's quote screen is ems alone, the venue's adapter connectivity alone, and a vendor offering both in one plugin holds both. The order still comes from portfolio and is worked by oms. The request's parameters, its due, firm-until and expiry times among them, are standard fields of the order path, converted by the connectivity plugin at the edge, never a venue's extras.
examples.deployment_needs: a portfolio plugin to decide and an oms plugin to work the order

needs.pending: the order path's revisions, after the book's
the bond template, after the template mechanism

examples.available: With the order path's revisions, and a bond's terms with its template. A price in percent of par is a gap in the contract today, which an agent names.

examples.why: Reconciling the book with the street, each difference a break, is operations'. If no plugin brings the broker's statement in, custody too, preferably an existing custody plugin, so the custodian's view and the check on it are in separate hands.
examples.deployment_needs: a custody plugin bringing the broker's statements in
examples.available: The street's statements and positions at v7; the book at v8, its opening balance refused from v9 until every required field is supplied; from v14 the custodian's activity, which explains a break and proposes its adjustment for a person to confirm, and each connection's sync status, so a connection needing a person to sign in again is told apart from data merely old.

examples.why: Alerts are compliance's, and they are the kernel's records: it hears orders, executions, bookings and positions. Not reporting, which records no alert.
examples.available: Orders and executions from v22, the order path's first revision; bookings and the alert from v24, booking's revision; the compliance language's first terms, restrictions and limits, with v26.

examples.request: Make my book match my broker automatically
examples.reshaped_to: operations reconciles, records each difference as a break, and resolves one by an adjustment entry with its reason, which a person can review.
examples.why: As asked it needs the book's positions written from the street, a grant no role has.

examples.request: Let my plugin give my analyst access to account X
examples.reshaped_to: The plugin's page says what to ask for; a deployment admin grants the analyst read on the plugin and the account in the dashboard.
examples.why: As asked it needs to administer the deployment's access, which no plugin may.

examples.request: Read the raw broker responses my custody plugin keeps
examples.reshaped_to: If the information matters beyond that plugin, it is proposed for the contract in terms that name no vendor; until then it stays with its plugin and its page.
examples.why: Another plugin's storage is never a channel.
examples.available: Only by a revision of the contract.
